instructions: miniauth: a small identity server in Go with PostgreSQL. It signs users in, keeps browser sessions, issues personal access tokens, and answers a reverse proxy's forward-auth check. Login methods live in internal/providers/<name>. AGENTS.md is the source of these rules. Test files (*_test.go, testdata/) and local dev files (compose.yaml, compose/, Taskfile.yml, .github/) are out of scope for the secret and constant-time rules: they hold fixed test passwords on purpose.

rules.rule: In production Go and SQL code, a secret (password, session id, personal access token, flow secret, reset or invite token, TOTP secret, recovery code, provider client secret, SMTP password) MUST NOT reach a log line, an error message, a URL, a span attribute, or a database column in clear text. The database stores a hash of each session id and each token. A return URL that the user asked for is not a secret.

Production code that compares a secret or a hash of a secret with a value from a request MUST use crypto/subtle. Out of scope: test files, a check against the zero value, and a database lookup by hash.

Domain-driven design: each entity, value object, id, and DTO has its own named type. A bare string, []byte, or uuid.UUID MUST NOT carry a domain concept in an exported signature or a struct field of production code. A DTO stays in its adapter package (internal/api).
Each schema change is a new numbered migration file in migrations/. A diff MUST NOT edit or delete a migration file that already exists on the base branch.
SQL lives in queries/*.sql and goes through sqlc. Production Go code MUST NOT build or hold SQL strings.
HTML pages are templ components in internal/views that use the one stylesheet internal/views/assets/app.css. No inline style attribute, no <style> block, no inline <script>, no other CSS file.
Use the standard library first: net/http routing, log/slog. A new dependency in go.mod is allowed only when the standard library has no equal.
A comment states an invariant or an outside assumption. A comment MUST NOT say what the code says. Code MUST NOT contain ticket ids or links to tasks or docs.

This repo is public. Nothing names a real host, server, or deployment of the owner: tests and docs use example.test hosts or localhost. Public identity providers that the code must call (Google, Telegram) and public registries (ghcr.io) are allowed.
Docs and comments use simple English (ASD-STE100): short sentences, RFC 2119 keywords for obligations.
